primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Familial glucocorticoid deficiency type 1 due to MC2R loss-of-function (ACTH resistance)
mechanism: MC2R is the adrenal ACTH receptor and signals predominantly through Gs to adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, and protein kinase A in zona fasciculata cells to promote cortisol steroidogenesis. Loss of MC2R function therefore produces ACTH resistance with low cortisol and compensatory high ACTH. Mineralocorticoid secretion is classically preserved because aldosterone production in the zona glomerulosa is regulated primarily by angiotensin II and extracellular potassium through calcium-dependent signaling rather than by ACTH.
vignette: A 5-year-old boy is evaluated after several episodes of fasting hypoglycemia during febrile illnesses. He has diffuse hyperpigmentation of the skin and oral mucosa. Blood pressure is normal. Laboratory studies show a very low morning cortisol concentration, markedly elevated ACTH, normal serum sodium and potassium concentrations, and normal plasma renin activity and aldosterone concentration. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in MC2R.
lead: Which of the following signaling patterns best explains the combination of glucocorticoid deficiency and preserved mineralocorticoid secretion in this patient?
correct: Reduced ACTH-stimulated Gs–adenylyl cyclase–cAMP signaling in zona fasciculata with preserved angiotensin II- and potassium-dependent calcium signaling in zona glomerulosa
distractors: Reduced angiotensin II–AT1 receptor Gq/calcium signaling in zona glomerulosa with preserved ACTH-stimulated cAMP signaling in zona fasciculata
Failure of StAR-mediated cholesterol transfer into mitochondria throughout all steroidogenic zones of the adrenal cortex
Loss of 21-hydroxylase activity with diversion of steroid precursors toward adrenal androgen synthesis
Failure of pituitary POMC processing with reduced ACTH secretion and intact adrenal responsiveness to ACTH
distractor_notes: Impaired angiotensin II signaling in zona glomerulosa would reduce aldosterone secretion and tend to increase renin and disturb sodium/potassium homeostasis. This patient instead has normal renin and aldosterone with isolated glucocorticoid deficiency.

Severe StAR dysfunction impairs the delivery of cholesterol to the inner mitochondrial membrane, compromising synthesis of multiple adrenal steroid classes rather than selectively disrupting ACTH responsiveness. It would not explain classically preserved mineralocorticoid secretion in an MC2R loss-of-function state.

21-hydroxylase deficiency is a steroidogenic enzyme defect that decreases cortisol and may decrease aldosterone while increasing ACTH and adrenal androgen production. It does not cause the isolated ACTH-receptor signaling defect with normal aldosterone described here.
A defect in ACTH synthesis or POMC processing would produce low or inappropriately normal ACTH rather than the marked ACTH elevation and hyperpigmentation seen with peripheral ACTH resistance.
key_expl: This patient has familial glucocorticoid deficiency type 1 caused by loss of the ACTH receptor MC2R. ACTH normally activates MC2R on zona fasciculata cells, coupling through Gs to adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, and protein kinase A to promote cortisol synthesis. Loss of MC2R therefore causes low cortisol despite markedly elevated ACTH. Aldosterone is classically spared because zona glomerulosa secretion is controlled mainly by the renin-angiotensin system and extracellular potassium: angiotensin II activates AT1 receptors coupled to Gq/11 and intracellular calcium signaling, and potassium depolarizes the cell membrane to increase calcium entry.
objective: Explain the isolated glucocorticoid deficiency of MC2R-mediated familial glucocorticoid deficiency: ACTH-Gs-cAMP signaling fails in zona fasciculata while angiotensin II/potassium control of zona glomerulosa preserves aldosterone secretion.
